records.issue_text: TestLogger.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/fake.go returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of the receiver, so tests asserting on the original fake's captured DebugLogs/InfoLogs/ErrorLogs see zero calls and can't verify LoggerMiddleware logging behavior
records.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go, the newly added method `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }` always returns a fresh `TestLogger` rather than the receiver `f`. In the same diff, LoggerMiddleware now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go), meaning any logs will be recorded on the new TestLogger instance, not the original fake injected into the middleware. That matches the finding: tests inspecting the original fake’s `DebugLogs/InfoLogs/ErrorLogs` will observe zero calls and won’t be able to verify logging behavior.

records.issue_text: Shared instance across all decorated clients in metrics_middleware.go:75-80 - NewMetricsMiddleware closure sets imw.next on a single shared instance, so multiple applications overwrite next and route all requests through the last-decorated client's chain (pre-existing bug)
records.rationale: In `NewMetricsMiddleware`, a single middleware instance is created once (`imw := newMetricsMiddleware(...)`) and the returned closure mutates that shared instance on each decoration: `imw.next = next; return imw` (see `metrics_middleware.go` around the shown lines in the diff). If the same `plugins.ClientMiddleware` value is applied to decorate multiple clients, they will all share `imw` and overwrite `imw.next`, causing requests to route through the last-decorated `next` chain. This shared mutable state matches the finding’s mechanism.

records.issue_text: LoggerMiddleware short-circuits stream methods while ContextualLoggerMiddleware enriches them; the asymmetric split between similarly-named middlewares invites future duplication/confusion without clarifying doc comments
records.rationale: The finding claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware enriches stream methods while LoggerMiddleware short-circuits them. In the diff, ContextualLoggerMiddleware does *not* enrich stream methods: `SubscribeStream`, `PublishStream`, and `RunStream` all directly pass through without calling `instrumentContext`, e.g. `func (m *ContextualLoggerMiddleware) SubscribeStream(...){ return m.next.SubscribeStream(ctx, req) }` (same for PublishStream/RunStream). Therefore the described asymmetric behavior for stream methods is contradicted by the diff.
records.stripped_text: LoggerMiddleware short-circuits stream methods while ContextualLoggerMiddleware enriches them; the asymmetric split between similarly-named middlewares invites future duplication/confusion without clarifying doc comments
